day.text: Kookaburra. I visited Finley. Drew visited me, so I was confused, and my +1 is Finley's Turkey egg. Finley, you did have a visitor: me. That means Casey's story is false. day.note: I visited Finley. If Finley is the Turkey, that explains my +1. Drew's visit confused me, so my "Pigeon" result is unreliable. Casey says she visited Finley and saw no visitors, but I was there, and a Turkey would have given her an egg. Casey is lying.

day.text: Owl. I visited Casey and I was ALSO hugged. Blair and I both visited Casey and both got hugged, so Casey is the Floofer. Also, Casey says they visited Finley, but Finley is the Turkey. day.note: I'm badly exposed. I'll make a weak deflection onto Alex and stay away from Finley so I don't drag my partner down with me.

day.text: Agreed, it's Casey. Two of the people who visited Casey got hugged, and an Eagle visiting the Turkey would be +1, not +0. Let's vote. CAW.
day.note: Casey's story falls apart: two hugged visitors, and an Eagle visit to the Turkey would have given +1. Push for the vote.

day.text: Casey, your Eagle claim is already dead because of the Turkey egg, with or without me. Let's vote.
day.note: Casey is clearly caught, so push the vote.

day.text: Casey can't explain the +0 from visiting a Turkey. I'm voting Casey. CAW.
day.note: Casey is clearly Meowfia, so I'll caw.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.confusing: Confusion in round 3 confused me. Finley's confused report made him draw a real card, so his public nest showed +1 when no egg had actually been laid. The table, me included, read that +1 as a Turkey egg and used it to convict an innocent Farm player.
Alex.fun: My favourite moment was round 3 as the Sphinx. Blair's Hawk hit had caught me, but by claiming Owl and confirming Ellis's hug I got Casey and Ellis to trust me, and then I steered the vote onto Finley.
Alex.change: I would have a confused player's public nest change match the real effect, or have the Storyteller mark nest changes caused by confusion. As it stands, a confused Farm player's fake egg works as evidence against them that they can't answer.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I accused Blair of being the Floofer. Casey shot that down quickly, since Drew would have been hugged, and it nearly made me look like a cat covering. From the start I would have pushed Finley's unexplained +1 and left Blair alone.

Blair.confusing: How confusion affects nest counts. The rules say a confused player draws as the false report says, so Finley's real +1 could have been a 0. The table assumed a confused player's +1 still needed a real egg source, and that misreading got an innocent player eggsecuted.
Blair.fun: In round 2, I called out Finley with my Tit hit and got winked right away. That proved my read was right, and I still banked 22 points even though I was dead.
Blair.change: I'd make the confusion rule clearer. It should say outright whether the public nest count shows the true change or the false reported one, because players rely on nest counts so heavily.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I spent my persuasion on Alex. I should have pushed Drew harder, since I knew for certain his missed-Hawk-guess story was made up, and I should have explained that confusion can fake a nest change. Clearing Finley might have swung the vote and won Farm the round.

Casey.confusing: The Confused rule: a confused player draws what their false report says, so their public nest change can be fake too. The table, including me for most of the day, treated Finley's +1 as a real egg that needed a source.
Casey.fun: Round 2: Blair collapsed right after naming Finley as the Mouser, which pretty much confirmed it, and my 3 highest cards banked for 33.
Casey.change: Show the confusion caveat next to the nest-size list (for example, flag that a confused player's change may not be real) so the table doesn't treat confused counts as hard evidence.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I pushed Finley and called the first CAW, which helped get a Farm player eggsecuted. I should have said out loud that confusion explains Finley's +1, pointed the table at Alex and Drew, and held off on CAW. Instead I only switched my own throw, privately.

Drew.confusing: The Kookaburra being "confused" in round 3 was hard to follow: Finley's nest really went up by one, and it wasn't clear how much of a confused report can be trusted. Also, the eggsecution prompt said a Meowfia stake banks only if the eggsecuted Farm player was the target, but the result then called it "doubled by the Grudge", which the rules never mention.
Drew.fun: My favourite moment was round 3. As the Floofer, Alex and I steered the table onto Finley, who was actually Farm, even though Blair's true Hawk hit had pointed straight at Alex.
Drew.change: I'd make it clearer how confusion interacts with real egg changes, for example by telling the confused player whether the egg they drew was real.
Drew.regret: In round 3 my fake Tit claim said I guessed Hawk on Blair and missed. Blair really was the Hawk, so that set up a direct contradiction that nearly exposed me. I should have claimed a vaguer guess, like Pigeon on Blair, which no claim could disprove.

Ellis.confusing: The rule that a confused player 'still draws or discards as the report says.' It means a confused nest change can be fake. I missed that and told the table Finley's +1 was real, which was wrong. It cost us round 3.
Ellis.fun: In round 1, my visit to Finley gave me a Turkey egg. That proved Casey's Eagle story, 'no visitors at Finley,' was false, and my first big throw banked 34 points.
Ellis.change: When a player is confused, show the table whether their nest change was real or caused by the confusion. Right now the confusion rule lets real evidence and fake evidence look the same, and it's easy to misread.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I trusted Alex's Owl report because it matched my hug, and I brushed off Blair's Hawk egg on Alex and Drew's suspicious 'missed Tit guess.' I should have thrown at Alex or Drew. I also shouldn't have told the table that confusion can't change your nest.

Finley.confusing: The confusion rule in round 3 was the most confusing part. A confused player still draws cards as their wrong report says, so my nest really went up by one even though, as it turned out, nobody had laid an egg. The table took that +1 as hard proof I had visited the Turkey, and I couldn't clearly argue that the confusion had put the card there.
Finley.fun: I liked the round 3 eggsecution. I was sure to be eggsecuted, but I still threw my three best cards at Alex, the cat, and banked 33 points even though my side lost.
Finley.change: I'd make it public, or at least easy to state, that a confused player's egg change can come from the confusion itself. As it is, a confused Farm player's own nest size frames them and they can't defend against it.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I should have opened by explaining exactly how the rule works: a confused player still draws whatever the wrong report says, so my +1 wasn't real evidence. I should have kept pointing out that nobody else could explain a visit to me. Instead I let Ellis's "confusion only changes the report" go unchallenged, and that lost Farm the round.

review.title: The Phantom Egg
review.headline: A confused Kookaburra's fake egg gets him eggsecuted while two cats walk free.
review.summary: The Farm caught the cats quickly in rounds 1 and 2. In round 1 the Floofer's passive hug gave Casey away. In round 2 Blair's Tit guess named Finley as the Mouser outright. Round 3 was the real game. Blair's true Hawk hit outed Alex, but Drew invented a missed Tit guess on Blair to cancel it. Alex then faked an Owl report that matched Ellis's hug, and the table believed it. Finley's +1 came only from being confused, but everyone treated it as a real egg, and he was eggsecuted as Farm. Alex won on a 40-point double bank. Ellis led after two rounds and scored nothing in the last one.

rounds.recap: Casey (Floofer) claimed Eagle and said she visited Finley. Her partner Finley had claimed Turkey, so an Eagle visit should have shown her +1, and she was +0. Blair and Alex had both visited Casey and both been hugged. Casey was eggsecuted with five votes, and the Farm banked big.

Blair's Tit visited Finley, named Mouser, and got the egg. Nothing else could explain her +1. Finley claimed Owl and winked Blair after she had already made her case. The wink only confirmed it, and Finley was eggsecuted with Drew quietly voting alongside the table.

Blair's Hawk egg pointed at Alex. Drew claimed a missed Tit guess of Hawk on Blair to make her look like a liar. Alex's fake Owl report confirmed Ellis's hug and earned trust. Finley's +1 was a confusion artifact, but the table read it as a Turkey egg. Finley got 3 votes to Alex's 2 and was eggsecuted as Farm.

highlights.text: Finley's safe Turkey claim accidentally sank his partner, because it broke Casey's story that she visited Finley as the Eagle and saw nobody.
Blair named Mouser on her Tit visit and was right, and Finley's wink on her only confirmed it.
Alex had seen nothing, but he guessed from Ellis's claim that a Floofer had hugged him and reported 'saw the Floofer at Ellis', which won over Ellis and Casey.
Casey worked out in private that Finley's +1 was a confusion egg and switched to Alex, but she never told the table.

confusions.what: Ellis knew he was confused but still read his +1 as a real Turkey egg from Finley. A confused report changes the count, so no egg had actually been laid.
Ellis said 'confusion changes what your report says, not the card you drew. Your +1 is real.' That is wrong: a confused player draws whatever the false report says, so the +1 needed no source.
Ellis said there was 'no Pigeon in play'. Pigeon is in the pool, and an unclaimed role doesn't prove it is absent.
During the day Casey said Finley's +1 'can only be my Turkey egg'. She saw only at the vote that confusion could explain it.
Drew said a confused report 'doesn't explain a nest that actually went up by one'. His private reasoning doesn't show whether this was a deliberate lie, but the table accepted it as the rule.

worked: Tit naming a cat role turned one guess into a public, checkable claim and made Blair the hero of round 2.
Round 3 showed real bluffing: the Meowfia made up role reports (Drew's Tit miss, Alex's Owl sighting) that fit public facts, and the table had to weigh them against Blair's true Hawk claim.
Stakes for the throwing Farm player bank whenever the target is Meowfia. Blair, Casey and Finley were each right about a cat and scored 25–33 even though their side lost. That rewards personal reads.
Being Meowfia shuffled the standings: Alex went from tied second to a clear win with one 2x bank.
problems: Confusion changes real nest sizes, but players treat a public +1 as proof of a real egg. This decided round 3 and misled Ellis in round 1. Fix: confused players shouldn't draw fake eggs, or the rules should say clearly that a confused +1 may have no source.

The round-win bonus (5) is tiny next to stakes of 20–40. Farm players threw for their own banks instead of coordinating. Blair threw at Drew, not Alex, and the Farm lost the vote. Raise the bonus or make it scale.

The Mouser's Wink gives itself away. Only the Mouser starts with one, so 'nobody learns who winked' means nothing, and a late wink confirms the accusation. Consider hiding which cat has the Wink, or allowing a Wink only before beat 2.

The Floofer's passive hug and the Tit's cat guess each solved a round in beat 1, so rounds 1 and 2 were never in doubt. Consider making the passive hug weaker or hiding it, and limiting the Tit to Farm role guesses.

Log and engine issues: debug text leaks ('no effect at tier 50'). Alex's hug is listed twice. In round 3, Farm players are labelled 'won' even though their side lost. The pool lists all 8 Farm animals, but the rule says Farm players + 3 = 7.
